root_idea.summary: The root expresses three principal orientations: directing oneself toward a goal, angry or forceful withholding, and turning aside or withdrawing.
root_idea.development: These orientations extend into deprivation or cessation, separation and solitude, and specialized descriptions of distortion, bodily impairment, rope structure, camel anatomy, and reed construction.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The sole Quran-attested group is presented under the normalized nominal citation form حَرْد.

senses.definition: Directed aim, purpose, or determined course toward an intended object.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction وَغَدَوْا عَلَى حَرْدٍ قَادِرِينَ, understood as setting out with a fixed aim or purpose.

senses.definition: Withholding or prevention of what is intended to be obtained.
senses.usage_conditions: In the same Quranic construction, an alternative interpretation understands حَرْد as withholding or preventing access, associated with sharpness or anger; this is a distinct classical reading of the verse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To separate oneself from others; to leave, abandon, or forsake one's people and withdraw to a place apart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes a person's withdrawal or removal from communal life.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become angry or exasperated, with a desire to kill the one who caused the anger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used with عَلَى for being angry with someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel or other beast: to suffer a foreleg tendon disorder that causes it to shake or strike the ground with the leg.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The condition concerns the forelegs and may result from a cord binding the fore shank to the arm.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a man: to be oppressed by the weight of his coat of mail, so that he cannot stretch himself out while walking.
Of a bowstring: to have one or more of its component portions longer than the others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description concerns unevenness among the strands or twisted portions of the string.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To twist or plait a rope so tightly that its strands knot and overlap; to roll it into a rounded form; also to bend or curve a thing into an arch.
To seek shelter or lodging in a hut with a gibbous roof.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction describes a person's resort to a particular kind of hut or covert.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become withholding or deficient: to yield little or no milk, or to cease supplying what is contained within.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Of a she-camel or woman, it concerns milk; of a vessel, its beverage; of a year, little rain. The same verb is also used of someone about to give and then refraining, and of a condition that changes into an unfamiliar or displeasing state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To separate, set apart, or remove someone or something.
Of a star: to dart downward.
Anger, or rancour and enmity retained in the heart while awaiting an opportunity to act on it.
An intestine or gut, especially the gut of a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is حُرُودٌ; a reported sense of “piece of a camel's hump” is explicitly rejected in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disease or fault of a camel's forelegs involving dryness or relaxation of the tendons and causing repeated shaking or striking of the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The condition is generally described as acquired rather than natural and affects the forelegs, not the hind legs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Uneven in its strands; especially a rope or bowstring whose twisted portions are not of equal length.
Needy or in want.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare descriptive use applied to a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bundle of reeds or canes laid across rafters in the construction of a roof.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is described as an Arabicized term and has the plural حَرَادِيّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A crosswise reed girdle or a set of reeds used on a reed fence or attached in bent form to the arched branches of a grapevine to support its shoots.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are specialized uses in reed fencing and vine cultivation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man having wide or capacious intestines like those of a camel.
A she-camel yielding little milk or ceasing to yield milk.
The prominent edges, knots, or overlapping portions of a rope produced by very tight twisting of its strands.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same form also serves as the plural of حِرْد in the anatomical sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Solitary or separated from others; a person who withdraws from his people, or a single and isolated individual.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may describe a solitary person, a tribe that does not mix with others, or a solitary star.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tendon or sinew in the place where a foreleg may be bound to the arm, causing an affected beast to shake the leg while walking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The tendon may be naturally affected or may produce the condition called حَرَد.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Angry or exasperated; also, a compact, strong, formidable person or lion who appears angry because of disdainful bearing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The second description may denote someone feared or dreaded whose manner suggests anger.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel or other beast affected by the foreleg disease called حَرَد.
Oppressed by the weight of one's coat of mail and unable to walk with the body fully extended.
Niggardly, mean, or sordid; close-fisted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The close-fisted use is expressed with أَحْرَدُ اليَدَيْنِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Applied to a rope or bowstring: plaited or twisted so that it has prominent, distorted, or overlapping edges or strands.
A room, house, or hut roofed with reed bundles, especially one with a gibbous or arched roof.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may be used substantively for the room or house itself.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Directing or aiming, with a Quranic attestation.
Withholding or preventing, explicitly applied as a Quranic interpretation.
Animal impairment, armor burden, and uneven bowstring strands.
Tight twisting and rolling of a rope.
Bending or curving into an arch.
Cross-reference and editorial implication concerning حُرْدِيّ.
Seeking shelter in a gibbous-roofed hut.
Scant or ceased supply of milk.
Extended use for cessation of a woman's milk.
Extended use for a vessel lacking beverage.
Extended use for a year of little rain.
Refraining after being about to give.
Separating or removing someone or something.
The nominal synonym حَرْدٌ = قَصْدٌ is covered by the Quranic aim sense.
General intestine sense and plural information.
She-camel yielding little or no milk.
Prominent edges and knots in a tightly twisted rope.
Plural relation to the gut sense.
Solitary or separated person, tribe, or star.
Room associated with reed roofing bundles.

cautions: The sole Quran occurrence, حَرْدٍ in 68:25, has competing classical interpretations: directed aim or determination, and withholding or prevention associated with anger. The supplied contextual gloss reflects the first reading but does not by itself establish the lexical senses.
